title: Sorting
description: Generates 2,000,000 integers with MINSTD, sorts them ascending with the standard library sort and prints first, last, median and a position-weighted checksum.
pseudocode:
x = seed
a = array of 2,000,000 integers, each from x = x * 48271 mod (2^31 - 1)
sort a ascending                         # standard library sort
print a[0], a[last], a[middle]
print sum over i of (i + 1) * a[i]       # position-weighted checksum
reveals: Comparison and memory-access efficiency of the default sort.
caveat: Algorithm and stability differ (introsort, pdqsort, timsort, V8 typed-array sort). Node uses Int32Array.sort and Python list.sort on plain ints - the idiomatic fast path of each. Haskell sorts a linked list with Data.List.sort and OCaml uses Array.stable_sort; Elixir sorts a list with Enum.sort.
